posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
Your code mentioned ChatGPT. Can you quickly tell us how much of your code is AI-generated and which is your work?
RPG maker's code isn't really flexible regarding map manipulation during runtime. I recommend looking into this plugin because it's free and simple to use, and I think you can learn a bit about how it works just by looking into the code directly.
Tile Changer (Shaz's plugin for MV ported to MZ)
Shaz_TileChangerMZ.js by Shaz (original plugin) and SeaPhoenix (edits for MZ)  Prologue @Shaz has a great plugin to copy tiles and change tiles for MV, and I got their approval to port this plugin to MZ. The main edits are for compatibility, especially in terms of the plugin commands, and...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
At first sight, I think the problem is that your code does not update the graphic layer. So the game map holds the new tiles, but the graphic layer doesn't.
Alternatively, here's a list of plugins that I know that can manipulate the map (most/all of them commercially)
-
https://drag-and-plug-in.itch.io/sandbox-map-for-mz
-
https://aerosys.blog/sandbox-engine
-
https://notritter.itch.io/ritter-map-transform-plugin-rpg-maker-mz
-
https://visustellamz.itch.io/tile-grafter-system

gstv87
posts.body:
well, the thing with maps is that they're just a bunch of numbers, not the bitmap you see.
the map data is what you should be looking at, so when rendering a map (on it's own, or on top of another) you just have to *render whatever that chunk of numbers says*
"that chunk of numbers", is the map table, brought from the other map.
the "building", you make with the same code from the same map you're in.... you just swap the thing it'll be looking at.
and when it comes to loading another map on top of yours, you just duplicate the destination object (the layers), so as to not overwrite yours.
*all* of that, is code that already exists... you just have to redirect it correctly.
writing all of that spaghetti as it was, is something AI would do... because >*AI DOESN'T KNOW OF CONTEXT*<
it doesn't know that you already HAVE the code but don't know where to look.
all of this, I figured out on my own, in Ace, six months ago.
you can look in my profile, that I rewrote the Tilemap object, for this very purpose
